text.p: Germany's third-largest commercial bank, Commerzbank AG said on Tuesday it expected to post a "satisfactory" result for 1996, which would enable it to pay a dividend while strengthening bank reserves.

The bank's chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen has already been quoted in a newspaper interview last week as saying Commerzbank did not plan to raise its dividend pay-out for 1996 from the 13.50 marks ($8.94) paid in 1995 in order to boost reserves.
Commerzbank in the first nine months posted a 49 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 1.68 billion marks, a level which already exceeded the full year 1995 pre-tax profit of 1.19 billion marks.
Operating profit before provisions rose 36.9 percent to 1.67 billion marks compared with the year-ago period, below analysts' expectations for a figure of 1.8 billion marks.
The operating profit figure fell below analysts' forecasts, which had averaged 1.8 billion marks and ranged from 1.71 billion marks to 1.92 billion.

Commerzbank said that given an expected tax ratio of around 40 percent, the after-tax profit should be roughly one billion marks, which translates into a return-on-equity of just over 11 percent after tax and 18.7 percent before tax.
Kohlhaussen said his bank was "relaxed" about the current discussion about bank mergers in Germany. "We are watching discussions with interest, but in a relaxed way," Kohlhaussen said.
"This bank is strong, but well-equipped -- materially, mentally and professionally -- to go its own way, as it has done for the last 126 years," Kohlhaussen said.
A precondition for the successful survival in the banking market of the future was a healthy foundation which would be strengthened by this year's results, Kohlhaussen said.
Innovation and flexibility were further preconditions for independence, he said.
Kohlhaussen said that it expected better own-account trading results for 1996 and said that share market trading in the third quarter did not follow a successful course.

He said the share market trading group for the first nine months of the year reported a profit of only 66 million marks compared with 402 million marks in the year-ago period, but he expected better profits in the fourth quarter.
Commerzbank is the last of the Big Three Frankfurt banks to publish nine-month results and, as expected, managed to outshine its two larger rivals in terms of earnings growth.

Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank and the only one to publish its results under International Accounting Standards, said its net profit grew nine percent to 1.5 billion marks while operating profit jumped 25.8 percent to 3.49 billion marks.
Dresdner Bank AG, the country's Number Two bank, reported a 29.7 percent rise in operating profit, a slowdown from 44 percent reported after the first six months.
